questions.subtopic: Size Reduction: laws of size reduction
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the laws of size reduction are CORRECT?

options.A: Rittinger's law states that the energy required for size reduction is proportional to the new surface area created.
options.B: Kick's law states that the energy required is proportional to the logarithm of the size reduction ratio.
options.C: Bond's law states that the energy required is inversely proportional to the square root of the product particle size (and directly related to the reduction achieved).
options.D: Rittinger's, Kick's, and Bond's laws give identical energy predictions for all size-reduction ratios.

questions.solution:
Q.59 Solution:• Correct Answer: A, B, C• Section: Agricultural Process Engineering | Sub-topic: Size Reduction: laws of size reduction | Type: MSQ | Marks: 2Q.59   Size Reduction: laws of size reductionType & Marks: MSQ — 2 marksQuestion:Which of the following statements regarding the laws of size reduction are CORRECT?(A) Rittinger's law states that the energy required for size reduction is proportional to the new surface area created.(B) Kick's law states that the energy required is proportional to the logarithm of the size reduction ratio.(C) Bond's law states that the energy required is inversely proportional to the square root of the product particle size (and directly related to the reduction achieved).(D) Rittinger's, Kick's, and Bond's laws give identical energy predictions for all size-reduction ratios.Answer: A, B, CDetailed Explanation:Rittinger's law (A) relates energy to newly created surface area, making it suitable for fine grinding. Kick's law (B) relates energy to the ratio of initial to final particle size on a logarithmic basis, suited to coarse crushing. Bond's law (C) — the most widely used — expresses energy in terms of the work index and the difference of reciprocal square roots of final and initial sizes. (D) is false: the three laws are empirical approximations valid over different size ranges and do not agree with one another in general.

questions.subtopic: Heat and Mass Transfer: heat exchanger configurations
questions.question: Which of the following statements about heat exchangers used in dairy and food processing are CORRECT?

options.A: For the same terminal temperatures, the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) of a counter-current exchanger is generally higher than that of a co-current (parallel-flow) exchanger.
options.B: In a parallel-flow (co-current) heat exchanger, the outlet temperature of the cold fluid can exceed the outlet temperature of the hot fluid.
options.C: Plate heat exchangers generally provide a higher heat transfer coefficient per unit floor area than shell-and-tube exchangers.
options.D: Fouling on heat transfer surfaces decreases the overall heat transfer coefficient.

questions.solution:
Q.63 Solution:• Correct Answer: A, C, D• Section: Agricultural Engineering | Sub-topic: Heat and Mass Transfer: heat exchanger configurations | Type: MSQ | Marks: 2Q.63   Heat and Mass Transfer: heat exchanger configurationsType & Marks: MSQ — 2 marksQuestion:Which of the following statements about heat exchangers used in dairy and food processing are CORRECT?(A) For the same terminal temperatures, the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) of a counter-current exchanger is generally higher than that of a co-current (parallel-flow) exchanger.(B) In a parallel-flow (co-current) heat exchanger, the outlet temperature of the cold fluid can exceed the outlet temperature of the hot fluid.(C) Plate heat exchangers generally provide a higher heat transfer coefficient per unit floor area than shell-and-tube exchangers.(D) Fouling on heat transfer surfaces decreases the overall heat transfer coefficient.Answer: A, C, DDetailed Explanation:(A) is correct: counter-flow arrangements maintain a more uniform temperature difference along the length of the exchanger, giving a higher LMTD than parallel flow for the same terminal temperatures. (B) is false: this crossing of outlet temperatures is a distinguishing feature of counter-current exchangers, not parallel-flow ones — in parallel flow the cold-fluid outlet temperature can never exceed the hot-fluid outlet temperature, since both fluids move in the same direction and approach a common temperature asymptotically. (C) is correct: the thin plates and highly turbulent, narrow flow channels of plate exchangers give much higher area-specific heat transfer coefficients than shell-and-tube designs. (D) is correct, since fouling deposits add an additional thermal resistance in series, reducing the overall coefficient.
